research_question: What evidence explains why dogs tilt their heads, and when can the behaviour be a sign of a medical problem?

sources.title: Why Do Dogs Tilt Their Heads?
sources.reliability: Canine organization educational article; secondary source
notes: Head tilting may have multiple possible explanations, including attention and sound processing.
The gesture should be interpreted in context rather than assigned a fixed meaning.

sources.title: Why do dogs tilt their heads?
sources.reliability: University news portal; topic-specific article needs verification
notes: University reporting can provide context on canine cognition research; use alongside primary studies.

sources.title: Dogs' head tilting and word learning
notes: Research on gifted word-learning dogs found more head tilting when they heard names of familiar toys.
The sample is specialized and does not establish a universal explanation.

sources.title: Canine hearing and communication
notes: Ear and vestibular disorders can affect balance and head position.
Persistent abnormal head tilt with additional symptoms warrants veterinary assessment.

sources.title: Dog behaviour and body language
notes: Dog body language should be read in context and alongside other signals.
Behaviour and welfare observations should avoid overinterpreting a single gesture.
